rules.title: Utility payment defense to nonpayment eviction
rules.requirement: A tenant may not be evicted for nonpayment of rent if the tenant used the unpaid rent to keep utility services (electric, gas, water, sewer) going after notice of discontinuance, where the landlord was responsible for those utilities and did not pay. The money used counts as part of the rent payment.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants facing eviction for nonpayment where the landlord was responsible for paying electric, gas, water or sewer service.
rules.quoted_span: These utilities include electric, gas, water, and sewer. The money used to pay for the continuance of those services shall be considered a portion of the rental payment.

rules.title: Eviction for failure to pay rent increase; no unconscionable increases
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict for failure to pay a rent increase only after notice of the increase and a Notice to Quit served at least one month before filing; the increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with other laws and municipal ordinances, including rent control.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants given notice of a rent increase who fail to pay it.
rules.quoted_span: The rent increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including rent control.
rules.interaction_text: must comply with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including rent control

rules.title: Health and safety violation or removal from the rental market
rules.requirement: Where eviction is sought because of substantial health and safety violations, illegal occupancy, or a governmental agency permanently removing the property from the rental market, a Notice to Quit must be served at least three months before filing, and the tenant cannot be evicted until relocation assistance is provided.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants evicted under cause G (health and safety violations, illegal occupancy, government redevelopment).
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three months before filing a suit for eviction. The tenant can’t be evicted until relocation assistance is provided.

rules.title: Relocation assistance for illegal occupancy evictions
rules.requirement: A tenant evicted for illegal occupancy is entitled to relocation assistance equal to six times the tenant's monthly rent, paid by the landlord; if not paid at least five days before removal the tenant may receive payment from a municipal revolving relocation assistance fund, which the landlord must repay.
rules.key_value: six times the tenant’s monthly rent
rules.coverage_text: Tenants evicted under cause G 3) (illegal occupancy).
rules.penalty: If the municipality has no relocation assistance fund and the landlord does not pay in time, interest accrues on the unpaid balance at 18% per year until paid in full; the amount due is a lien on the property.
rules.quoted_span: Any tenant evicted under G 3) (illegal occupancy) is entitled to relocation assistance in an amount equal to six times the tenant’s monthly rent.

rules.title: Permanent retirement of property from residential use
rules.requirement: A landlord permanently retiring a building or mobile home park from residential use may evict only after serving a Notice to Quit at least 18 months before filing, and no legal action may be taken until the lease expires.
rules.coverage_text: Buildings or mobile home parks being permanently retired from residential use, where cause G does not apply.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least 18 months prior to filing the suit for eviction.

rules.title: Conversion to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership
rules.requirement: A landlord converting a building or mobile home park to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership must serve a Notice to Quit at least three years before filing and may not act until the lease expires; courts grant up to five one-year stays if no comparable housing was offered, and protected senior or disabled tenants may not be evicted while protected status lasts.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants of buildings or mobile home parks being converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership of two or more units or park sites.
rules.exemptions: Not more than a one-year stay if the landlord gives five months' free rent; no action against senior citizen or disabled tenants with protected tenancy status.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be ser ved on the tenant at least three years before filing a suit for eviction.

rules.title: Owner move-in or sale in buildings of three units or less
rules.requirement: The owner of a building with three residential units or less may evict to personally occupy a unit or to sell to a buyer who will occupy it, after serving a Notice to Quit at least two months before filing; no legal action until the lease expires.
rules.coverage_text: Buildings with three residential units or less.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least two months prior to filing suit for eviction. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(l)).

rules.title: Evictions for owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings
rules.requirement: Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only by court order on listed grounds (holdover, nonpayment, disorderly conduct, damage, rule violations, lease violations with right of re-entry); a three-month notice to quit is required for at-will or year-to-year tenancies and one month for month-to-month and other tenancies.
rules.quoted_span: Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only when a court issues an order for eviction.

rules.title: Rooming and boarding house evictions
rules.requirement: Owners of rooming and boarding houses must follow the good causes and notice requirements of the Eviction Law when evicting residents, unless otherwise ordered by the Bureau, and must give at least three working days' notice to the County Welfare Board before starting an eviction.
rules.coverage_text: Rooming and boarding houses: buildings with at least two living units occupied by unrelated persons without private kitchens and bathrooms, unless an exception in the Rooming and Boarding House Act applies.
rules.exemptions: Except if otherwise ordered by the Bureau; buildings meeting an exception in the Rooming and Boarding House Act.
rules.quoted_span: The Regulations Governing Rooming and Boarding Houses, which are enforced by the Bureau of Rooming and Boarding House Standards of the Department of Community Affairs, require owners of rooming and boarding houses to follow the good causes and notice requirements of the Eviction Law when evicting residents, except if otherwise ordered by the Bureau (N.J.A.C. 5:27-3.3(c)).
